title: Informative disorders in initial digital circulation news articles on ChatGPT (Trastornos informativos en notas periodísticas iniciales de circulación digital sobre ChatGPT)
screen_reason: Quantitative content analysis of a defined corpus of 78 Spanish-language digital news articles about ChatGPT, reporting the share of articles coded as exhibiting an information disorder (20 articles, 26% of 78) against an explicit denominator. Meets the CONTENT criterion (share of items in a sample classified false/misleading).

estimates.country: Iberoamérica; 50 of the 78 articles from Spain, the rest from Mexico, Colombia, Chile and England
estimates.platform: Digital news outlets and specialised technology/IT websites, harvested via Google Alerts
estimates.date: Alerts received 16 January to 14 February 2023 (articles published January-February 2023)
estimates.measure_type: % of digital news articles about ChatGPT coded as exhibiting an information disorder (mis-, dis- or mal-information)
estimates.value_raw: 20 informaciones o el 26% del total [20 items, or 26% of the total] (of 78 articles)
estimates.denominator: 78 Spanish-language digital news articles about ChatGPT (81 Google Alerts received 16 Jan-14 Feb 2023, 78 retained after inclusion criteria)
estimates.definition: An article counted in the numerator if the coding sheet classified it into one of the three Wardle & Derakhshan information-disorder types: información errónea / mis-information (false but not created with intent to harm), desinformación / dis-information (false, deliberately created to harm), información incorrecta / mal-information (based on real facts but used to harm).
estimates.misinfo_def: "todas las formas de información falsa, información inexacta o engañosa diseñada, presentada y promovida para causar daño público intencionalmente o para ganancia" [all forms of false, inaccurate or misleading information designed, presented and promoted to intentionally cause public harm or for profit] - the European Commission 2018 definition adopted by the authors
estimates.source_quote: examinadas, esto es 20 informaciones o el 26% del total,
estimates.page_loc: Section III (Resultados y discusión), pp. 4-5; Figs 1-2
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Researcher coding with a combined observation/coding sheet (hoja de observación/codificación) built on Wardle & Derakhshan's (2017) information-disorder typology as presented in a Council of Europe document, plus content analysis and discourse analysis, with nine descriptive indicators coded alongside. No number of coders, no coder training and NO intercoder reliability statistic are reported.
estimates.moderator_quote: Como unidad de análisis se tuvo a cada una de las informaciones sobre el ChatGPT recibidas en un mes al teléfono celular del investigador titular, desde el sistema de alertas de Google, que -en facultad de sus algoritmos- procesó el interés en el tema desde la primera semana de enero. Se recibieron, en total, 81 alertas entre el 16 de enero al 14 de febrero de 2023; se aplicó un filtro sobre la base de los criterios de inclusión que se señalan, dando como resultado 78 notas periodísticas. [The unit of analysis was each item about ChatGPT received over one month on the lead researcher's mobile phone from the Google alerts system, which - by its algorithms - processed interest in the topic from the first week of January. In total 81 alerts were received between 16 January and 14 February 2023; a filter based on the stated inclusion criteria was applied, giving 78 news items.]
estimates.notes: SOURCE QUOTE IS A FRAGMENT BY NECESSITY: the PDF text layer interleaves the article's two columns, so no full sentence of the Results is a contiguous verbatim span. The complete sentence reads: 'Sin embargo, una importante cuarta parte de las notas examinadas, esto es 20 informaciones o el 26% del total, todavía presentan características relacionadas con el concepto y praxis de los desórdenes informativos.' [However, an important quarter of the items examined, that is 20 items or 26% of the total, still present characteristics related to the concept and practice of information disorders.] The complement is stated too: '...encontraron desórdenes informativos: 58 notas o el 74% del total de la muestra evidenciaron manejarse en el marco de la verdad periodística' [58 items or 74% of the total sample were shown to operate within the frame of journalistic truth]. 20/78 = 25.6%, consistent with the verbatim 26%. BORDERLINE flagged because the umbrella 'information disorder' category includes mal-information, which the authors define as content 'con datos basados en la realidad' [with data based on reality] used to harm - i.e. a factually true item can receive the label - so the 26% is not purely a falsity share; 14 of the 20 (mis- + dis-information) are the explicitly false types. Topic coded science_other as the nearest available category for a technology/AI news corpus. platform_norm=web_cross_platform because the corpus spans many news and tech websites rather than one platform. denom_selection=curated: the corpus is whatever Google Alerts algorithmically pushed to one researcher's profile, not a census of Iberoamerican ChatGPT coverage (the authors nonetheless call it 'censal'). No reliability statistics, hence confidence=medium.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, and the adjudicator should see why: the paper's breakdown BY disorder type has the 20-article disorder subset as its denominator, not the 78-article corpus - 'Las informaciones incorrectas aparecieron en menor número: 06 notas o el 30%' [incorrect/mal-information items appeared in smaller number: 06 items or 30%] (6/20 = 30%), 'Se ha constatado la presencia de informaciones erróneas en la mitad de las notas que exponen trastornos informativos' [erroneous/mis-information items were found in half of the items showing information disorders] (10/20 = 50%, abstract: 'erroneous (10)'), and 'Finalmente, 4 notas de las 20 analizadas o el 20% fueron identificadas como desinformaciones' [finally, 4 of the 20 analysed items, or 20%, were identified as disinformation] (4/20 = 20%). These are R3-type within-misinformation breakdowns; I did not create rows for them because the three are mutually exclusive parts of the same 20 and selecting any one would be arbitrary, and re-basing mis+dis (14) on 78 would be a cross-category sum forbidden by R8. Note also the paper's loose wording 'de las 20 analizadas', which reads as if 20 were the whole sample; the corpus is 78. Also not extracted: the descriptive cross-tabulations that are not falsity shares (45/78 news format, 16/78 guide format, 50/78 from Spain, 59/78 signed, 40/78 from formal media, pragmatic intent 46%/35%/19%, stance 51% optimistic / 28% pessimistic / 21% neutral, and the same distributions inside the 20-article disorder subset). Figures 1-3 are images and carry no additional extractable numbers in the text layer.

rob.design: Exploratory mixed-methods (content + discourse analysis) census of the Google Alerts stream on ChatGPT reaching one researcher's phone: 81 alerts, 16 Jan-14 Feb 2023, 78 retained after inclusion criteria (on topic; written text; Spanish) and exclusion criteria (paywalled/restricted access; syndicated from other sites without recognised authorship; from sites of doubtful reliability). Coding instrument: a combined observation/coding sheet with the Wardle & Derakhshan three-type information-disorder typology plus nine descriptive indicators and an open qualitative column. Number of coders not stated; no intercoder reliability reported; no response rate applicable. The authors themselves flag the alert-driven sample as a limitation ('los resultados entregan una fotografía que ha de contrastarse con más tomas si se quisieran generalizar hallazgos' [the results give a snapshot that would have to be contrasted with further snapshots if one wanted to generalise findings]).
rob.item6_quote: El instrumento desplegado final se basó en la tipología ajustada por Wardle y Derakhshan en 2017, para catalogar desórdenes informativos en tres posibilidades: 1) información incorrecta, 2) información errónea y 3) desinformación, presentada en un documento del Council of Europe [11] [The final instrument deployed was based on the typology adjusted by Wardle and Derakhshan in 2017, to catalogue information disorders in three possibilities: 1) mal-information, 2) mis-information and 3) dis-information, presented in a Council of Europe document].
rob.item10_quote: Sin embargo, una importante cuarta parte de las notas examinadas, esto es 20 informaciones o el 26% del total, todavía presentan características relacionadas con el concepto y praxis de los desórdenes informativos. [However, an important quarter of the items examined, that is 20 items or 26% of the total, still present characteristics related to the concept and practice of information disorders.]
